clue.text: Maybe Wilson's endless patrol

indicators.note: endless asks for the final letter of the singer's surname to be cut off

parts.note: Wilson Pickett was an American soul singer, so his surname is one possible owner of the forename Wilson

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a patrol belongs to a man called Wilson, perhaps a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe Wilson's' points to the soul singer Wilson Pickett; 'endless' drops the last T of his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikers posted at a workplace gate form a patrol that watches who goes in, as do military guard pickets.

clue.text: Makes stroke with one iron to take no risks

parts.note: in golf or cricket a stroke is made when one plays
one is A, the indefinite article
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a shot with a single iron club to stay out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for acting cautiously and avoiding any gamble.

clue.text: Stays in French island resort to experiment

parts.note: Corse is the French name for Corsica, an island belonging to France
to try is to resort to an experiment, giving something a go

explanation.surface: Someone stays on Corsica at a resort to test a theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb about holidays, but it is the noun: the boned stiffeners in a corset.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are the stiffened bodices of old underwear, and the craft or collection of such garments is the term.

clue.text: Try hard to turn Marc Bolan's band electronic

parts.note: E is the standard short form of electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: to turn asks for the band's name to be read from right to left

parts.note: T. Rex was the 1970s glam rock band fronted by Marc Bolan

explanation.surface: A rock band strains to switch from glam guitar to an electronic sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' makes XERT from T. Rex, the glam rock group led by Marc Bolan, and E for electronic goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert yourself is to make a strenuous effort, a synonym of straining.

clue.text: Square bashing did for a rule for him

definitions.text: Square bashing did for a rule for him

indicators.note: bashing means the inserted word is knocked out of shape into a new order
for here means standing in place of, so one word takes the slot the abbreviation held

parts.note: taken as written, the word square
R is a standard abbreviation for rule
taken as written, the word did

explanation.surface: Endless drill on the parade ground made a rule-follower of this recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: DID goes 'for' (in place of) R, short for rule, in SQUARE, and 'bashing' knocks DID into DDI. Square bashing is British army slang for parade-ground drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A private soldier is the man drilled on the barrack square, and British slang calls him this.

clue.text: Six-hour periods when rent is due

definitions.meaning: a day split four ways gives stretches of six hours each, read literally
in England the four traditional days in the year on which rents and tenancies fall due

explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading, a quarter of 24 hours, is the joke; the real sense is the four English rent days.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Day, Midsummer, Michaelmas and Christmas are the English rent days; read literally each is a quarter of a day.

clue.text: See our way to get confused -ignore that

indicators.note: to get confused means the letters of the three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets lost trying to find a route, then tells listeners to disregard the remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash marks the definition off from the wordplay; 'to get confused' is the anagram signal, with 'way' and 'see' looking like plain prose about getting lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill-sergeant's command to cancel the last order, used generally to withdraw a remark.

clue.text: Spot flaw in crystal when fluorine's replaced by tritium

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter of the word for a flaw is swapped out for another

parts.note: a defect is a flaw, and in physics an irregularity in a crystal lattice is so called
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine
T is the chemical symbol for tritium, heavy hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab report on a crystal whose fluorine atoms have been swapped for tritium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' swaps the F of DEFECT for T, the symbol for tritium.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or discover it, a synonym.

clue.text: Stand close by river

parts.note: the close of something is its end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A building stands near the bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate or bear it, as in 'I can't stand it'.

clue.text: A desire to eat large amounts at one

parts.note: greed is an excessive appetite, especially for food

explanation.surface: A glutton's appetite is in harmony with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at one with someone means being in accord with them.

clue.text: Grant assistance taking time for lady columnist

parts.note: Cary Grant was a Hollywood film star

indicators.note: taking means the word for help takes a letter into itself

parts.note: aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A grant to help a female newspaper columnist meet her deadlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'columnist' looks like a journalist but means a column: a caryatid is a carved female figure holding up a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone woman serving as a pillar in Greek architecture, as on the Erechtheion in Athens.

clue.text: Club's best place for dancing two-steps taking Ecstasy

indicators.note: taking means the jumbled letters take in one more letter
dancing means the letters of the step name move about into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: E is the street name for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A nightclub's best spot for dancers who are on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a nightclub but is a golf club or bat; 'dancing' rearranges TWOSTEPS and 'taking' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on a bat, racket or golf club face that hits the ball most effectively.

clue.text: One in No 10 shirt's power not right for top-class football

parts.note: the Prime Minister, or Premier, lives at No 10 Downing Street

indicators.note: power not right means the letter for power takes the place of the letters for right

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister in a number ten football shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' puts P for power in place of RT (right) in SHIRT, giving SHIP. No 10 is the British Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Premier League was the top division of English football, often called by this name.

clue.text: Sore about some obscure clue

indicators.note: about means the run of letters is turned round to read backwards
some means only part of the letters of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A solver is irritated by a baffling clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes RECLU from obscuRE CLUe, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An open sore on skin or a mucous membrane, such as a mouth or stomach lesion.

clue.text: Most serious undergraduate's aspiration

definitions.meaning: the gravest category of murder or burn in law and medicine
the top class of honours a British student hopes to graduate with

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'first' is the highest class of university honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder or burns of the gravest category, and the top British honours award, a 'first'.

clue.text: Like Bond's work to deal with SPECTRE

indicators.note: deal with suggests cards being dealt out and reshuffled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: James Bond's mission is to tackle the villainous organisation SPECTRE.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal with' rearranges TO and SPECTRE; SPECTRE is Bond's enemy organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy's missions are classified at the highest level of security.

clue.text: Place associated with living in sin a newspaper covered

indicators.note: covered means the word for sin wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: vice is sin or wickedness
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid exposes a scandal of a couple living together unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living' is not cohabiting but a church living, the post of a parish priest, whose house this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest's benefice is called a living, and the house that goes with it is his home.

clue.text: Somewhere primarily associated with certain article — glass

definitions.text: Somewhere primarily associated with certain article — glass

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the is the definite article, so certain article gives the word itself
a lens is a piece of shaped glass

explanation.surface: A place best known for being linked with one product, glass.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helens in Lancashire is famous as the home of Pilkington glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancashire town is known for glassmaking, the home of Pilkington.

clue.text: Who has inclination to follow what's formerly on letter?

definitions.text: Who has inclination to follow what's formerly on letter?

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the preceding piece
to follow means the word for inclination comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
late means formerly, as in the late chairman
a list is a lean or inclination, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone who likes to track what used to be stuck on letters: old stamps.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes a stamp collector, whose hobby is following what was once stuck on letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp collector, whose interest is in what was formerly stuck on letters.

clue.text: Emmanuel perhaps denied homeless woman's 14

indicators.note: denied means the woman is deprived of her degree, so those letters are removed from the front

parts.note: a bag lady is a homeless woman who carries her belongings in bags
the cross-reference to 14 across points to a first degree, a BA or Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A woman sleeping rough is refused the university qualification she wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' strips BA, a first degree (14 across), from BAG LADY'S. Nurse Gladys Emmanuel was the shopkeeper's sweetheart in the BBC sitcom Open All Hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel is the surname of the district nurse Gladys in the classic British TV comedy Open All Hours.

clue.text: Shakespearean girl having really hot body — not half

indicators.note: not half means one half of the long word, its first six letters, is dropped

parts.note: hyperthermia is the condition of a body being dangerously overheated

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine with a stunning figure, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops HYPERT, the first half of HYPERTHERMIA, a dangerously overheated body.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the young lovers in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a Shakespeare heroine.

clue.text: Superior Belgian city

definitions.meaning: a feudal lord to whom vassals owe allegiance
a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse

explanation.definitionFit: A feudal lord or overlord, and the French name of the city in Wallonia, Belgium.

clue.text: Send down corrupt fellow that's imprisoned

parts.note: to rust is to corrode or corrupt

indicators.note: imprisoned means the word for a fellow is held inside the abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
cat is old slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A corrupt man is sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send down' suggests prison, but at British universities it means to suspend a student temporarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge suspend an undergraduate from college for a time, which is to send them down.

clue.text: One American lawyer with house in western state

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A single US lawyer with a house out West.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state in the Rocky Mountain West, known for potatoes.

clue.text: Diplomatic initiative fixing border in river

indicators.note: in means the word for border is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a march is a borderland, as in the Welsh Marches

explanation.surface: Diplomats agree a frontier running down a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal diplomatic move or step, a French borrowing in English diplomatic language.

clue.text: Dish containing a relish

indicators.note: containing means the word for dish holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a plate is a dish

explanation.surface: A dish with a portion of chutney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like a condiment but means taste or liking.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's taste or liking for something, as in 'no palate for adventure'.

clue.text: Top-performing strikers new outfits

parts.note: star means leading or top-performing
tups are rams, which strike or butt with their heads

explanation.surface: Top football strikers are given new kits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikers' suggests footballers but means rams (TUPS), which butt.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly founded businesses; outfit is informal for a company.

clue.text: America's after cabbage plant

indicators.note: after means the abbreviation for America comes behind the vegetable

parts.note: cole is an old word for cabbage, as in coleslaw
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: The United States is chasing a cabbage plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical plant grown for its brightly coloured leaves.
